name: LA-03
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+18 partisan lean in a district Clay Higgins has held comfortably since 2017
Higgins's fundraising dominance: about $822,000 raised versus roughly $23,000 for the top Democrat
Prediction markets price a Republican win near 95%
No public polls or expert ratings; a low-attention race
model.rationale: The district's deep Republican lean, Higgins's incumbency and overwhelming financial edge, and prediction markets near 95% for the GOP all point the same way; with no contrary polling or ratings, the race remains firmly Safe R.
model.watch: A major scandal involving Higgins or an unusually strong national Democratic wave could narrow the margin, though nothing in the current evidence suggests either is likely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Southwest Louisiana's third district is one of the more Republican seats in the House, with a partisan lean of roughly eighteen points toward the GOP. Clay Higgins has held the seat since 2017 and runs again with the advantages of incumbency in a district that has consistently backed him by wide margins. He faces three Democratic challengers and one Republican, and Louisiana's jungle-primary format could extend the race to a runoff if no candidate reaches fifty percent in the first round.

Financial figures underline the imbalance: Higgins has raised about $822,000 and holds nearly $600,000 on hand, while the best-funded Democrat, John Day, has raised roughly $23,000. No outside groups have spent against the incumbent, no public polls have been conducted, and prediction markets price his reelection at roughly ninety-five percent. All available evidence points to a comfortable Republican hold.
